/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 33

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture33

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 33](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, `path(G) ≥ ⌈2 · dist_avg(M, V)⌉`, where `path(G)`
is the floor of the average distance of `G`, `M` is the set of maximum-degree vertices,
and `dist_avg(M, V)` is the average distance from all vertices to `M`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture33 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected),
      let M : Set α := {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}
      Int.ceil (2 * distavg G M) ≤ (path G : ℤ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The `path G` invariant cast to ℤ is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ (path G : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _

/-- In `K₃`, the max degree is 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).maxDegree = 2 := by decide

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture33

findings.description: The expression `distavg G M` on line 47 uses the wrong averaging operation. It computes `(∑ v, min_{m ∈ M} dist(v,m)) / |V|`, including zero contributions from vertices in M. The source instead averages all nonzero distances `dist(m,v)` with m ∈ M and v ∈ V. For connected graphs, its denominator is |M|·(|V|−1), and no minimum over M is taken. These give different per-graph bounds: on the perfect binary tree of depth 5, the path number is 11, the Lean average is 11/21 (giving the true bound 2 ≤ 11), and the source average is 1797/310 (giving the false bound 12 ≤ 11). Thus the fixed negative answer concerns a different inequality.
findings.source_evidence: DeLaVina's WOWII `all.html`, Conjecture 33, states `path(G) ≥ CEIL[2dist_avg(M,V)]`. Its definitions link invokes glossary entry 37 in http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js: “dist_avg(M,V) is the average of all nonzero dist_G(u,v) such that u is in M and and v is in V.” Read in the archived source at https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161735id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js .

findings.description: The docstring says `path(G)` “is the floor of the average distance of G.” The imported `SimpleGraph.path` actually counts vertices in a largest induced path, which is the source's intended invariant. This is an incorrect description, not an additional defect in the Lean path expression.
findings.source_evidence: WOWII glossary entry 35, linked by Conjecture 33, defines `path(G)` as “The number of vertices of a largest induced path of the graph.” See http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js, archived at https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161735id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js .
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “is the floor of the average distance of G” with “is the number of vertices of a largest induced path of G.” Leave the imported `SimpleGraph.path` definition unchanged.

sources_consulted: E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, cited index and menu: https://web.archive.org/web/20260807053017if_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/ and its linked menu.htm.

E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 33 and its October 2005 counterexample note: https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161800/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html (retrieved through https://r.jina.ai/http://wayback.archive.org/web/20260723161800/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html).

E. DeLaVina, WOWII glossary, especially entries 16, 35 and 37: https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161735id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js (retrieved through Microlink's public page-extraction API).
FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/VertexDistance.lean, definitions of isInducedPath, path, distToSet and distavg, and the computable-distance equivalence.
Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Finite.lean, Metric.lean, and Connectivity/Connected.lean; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean and Attributes/Basic.lean.
review.notes: The source marks Conjecture 33 false and records an October 2005 counterexample with path number 7 and average distance 3.56, so `research solved` and `answer(False)` have the correct status and polarity. Both sanity-check declarations are correct. The source glossary was recovered from archived copies because the legacy hosts were unavailable directly. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` compiles successfully and checks empty/singleton/two-vertex boundaries, nonemptiness of the maximum-degree set, the distinction between the two averages, the binary-tree averages and rounded bounds, and the proposed corrected statement's type. The binary tree's path number 11 follows from its diameter 10. No repository files were edited.

demonstrated.claim: On the connected graph K₂, using the declaration’s exact maximum-degree set M, SimpleGraph.distavg G M equals 0, whereas the source’s average over nonzero M-to-V pairwise distances equals 1.

submission.summary: Created /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean with a short concrete example demonstrating the wrong averaging definition, without claiming to prove or refute the entire negative-answer theorem. The required compile command reports no errors or warnings; the file uses no sorry or new axioms.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture33

/-!
WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture33.conjecture33:
On the connected graph K₂, the declaration's `distavg G M` is 0, whereas the
source's average of the nonzero distances from M to V is 1 (both distances are 1).
-/
example :
    let G : SimpleGraph (Fin 2) := ⊤
    let M : Set (Fin 2) := {v | SimpleGraph.degree G v = SimpleGraph.maxDegree G}
    SimpleGraph.Connected G ∧ SimpleGraph.distavg G M = 0 ∧
      (let pairs := (M.toFinset ×ˢ Finset.univ).filter
          (fun p => SimpleGraph.dist G p.1 p.2 ≠ 0)
       (∑ p ∈ pairs, (SimpleGraph.dist G p.1 p.2 : ℝ)) / (pairs.card : ℝ)) = 1 := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  refine ⟨by decide, ?_⟩
  have hM : ({v | SimpleGraph.degree (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) v =
      SimpleGraph.maxDegree (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2))} : Set (Fin 2)) = Set.univ := by
    ext v; fin_cases v <;> decide
  simp only [hM]
  norm_num [SimpleGraph.distavg, SimpleGraph.distToSet, SimpleGraph.dist_top,
    Finset.univ_fin2, Fin.sum_univ_two]
  have hp : ({p ∈ ({0, 1} : Finset (Fin 2)) ×ˢ {0, 1} | p.1 ≠ p.2}) =
      {(0, 1), (1, 0)} := by decide
  rw [hp]
  norm_num

submission.summary: Replaced the nearest-set distance average with the mean of all nonzero distances over M × V. Updated the docstring to describe this average and correctly identify path(G) as the largest induced-path order. Preserved the quantifiers, negative answer, status, and sanity checks. The required compilation succeeds with only the existing `sorry` warning.
